UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile and preferences within the ExpenseWise application, linked to an external authentication system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. This typically corresponds to the user's ID from an external authentication system.

username.description: The display name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user.

photoURL.description: The URL of the user's profile picture or avatar.

preferredCurrency.description: The currency preferred by the user for tracking expenses (e.g., 'INR', 'USD', 'EUR').

darkModeEnabled.description: Indicates if the user has enabled the dark mode interface preference.

budgetLimit.description: The optional monthly budget limit set by the user for spending tracking.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was last updated.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a classification for expenses (e.g., Food, Travel, Shopping).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

name.description: The descriptive name of the expense category (e.g., 'Food', 'Bills').

description.description: A brief explanation or context for the category.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile this category belongs to, allowing for user-defined categories. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Category)

PaymentMethod.title: PaymentMethod
PaymentMethod.description: Represents a method used for making an expense (e.g., Cash, Credit Card, Debit Card).

id.description: Unique identifier for the PaymentMethod entity.

name.description: The descriptive name of the payment method (e.g., 'Credit Card', 'Cash').

description.description: A brief explanation or details for the payment method.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile this payment method belongs to, allowing for user-defined payment methods. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N PaymentMethod)

Expense.title: Expense
Expense.description: Represents a single recorded financial expenditure by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Expense entity.

title.description: A short, descriptive name or summary for the expense.

amount.description: The monetary value of the expense.

expenseDate.description: The specific date when the expense occurred.

categoryId.description: Reference to the Category for this expense. (Relationship: Category 1:N Expense)

paymentMethodId.description: Reference to the PaymentMethod used for this expense. (Relationship: PaymentMethod 1:N Expense)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who recorded this expense. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Expense)

notes.description: Optional additional details or comments about the expense.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the expense record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the expense record was last updated.

definition.description: Stores the profile information and preferences for a specific user. The document ID (`{userId}`) for each UserProfile document MUST match the `id` field within the document, which in turn corresponds to the authenticated user's UID (`request.auth.uid`). This structure ensures direct ownership and simplified security rules.

params.name: userId
params.description: Unique identifier of the user, corresponding to `request.auth.uid` and the `id` field within the UserProfile document.

definition.description: Stores user-defined expense categories. Each category document includes a `userId` field which MUST match the `{userId}` in the path. This denormalization ensures authorization independence for security rules and allows for secure list operations, enabling users to only access their own categories.

params.name: userId
params.description: Unique identifier of the user who owns this category, matching the parent UserProfile and `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: categoryId
params.description: Unique identifier for the specific expense category.

definition.description: Stores user-defined payment methods. Each payment method document includes a `userId` field which MUST match the `{userId}` in the path. This denormalization ensures authorization independence for security rules and allows for secure list operations, enabling users to only access their own payment methods.

params.name: userId
params.description: Unique identifier of the user who owns this payment method, matching the parent UserProfile and `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: paymentMethodId
params.description: Unique identifier for the specific payment method.

definition.description: Stores individual expense records for a user. Each expense document includes a `userId` field which MUST match the `{userId}` in the path. This denormalization ensures authorization independence for security rules and allows for secure list operations, enabling users to only access their own expenses.

params.name: userId
params.description: Unique identifier of the user who recorded this expense, matching the parent UserProfile and `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: expenseId
params.description: Unique identifier for the specific expense record.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore data structure prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates. All user-specific data is organized under a top-level `/users` collection, with each user's data residing in a subcollection identified by their unique `userId`. This pattern provides strong authorization boundaries and simplified security rules.

**Authorization Independence:** Each entity (`UserProfile`, `Category`, `PaymentMethod`, `Expense`) includes a `userId` field. For `UserProfile`, its document ID is the `userId`. For `Category`, `PaymentMethod`, and `Expense`, the `userId` field within the document explicitly links it to its owner. Crucially, this `userId` field also appears as a wildcard (`{userId}`) in the document's path (e.g., `/users/{userId}/categories/{categoryId}`). This denormalization means that security rules can check ownership directly using `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId && resource.data.userId == userId` (where `userId` is the path segment wildcard) without needing to perform expensive and non-atomic `get()` operations on parent documents. This completely eliminates hierarchical authorization dependencies.

**Queryable Authorization Predicates (QAPs):** The structural segregation of data under `/users/{userId}/...` naturally enables secure `list` operations. Because all documents within, for example, `/users/{userId}/expenses` inherently belong to `{userId}`, a rule can simply `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. This ensures that a user can only list their own expenses, categories, or payment methods. There is no mixing of public and private data within these collections, maintaining a homogeneous security posture. The presence of `userId` in both the path and the document data provides a robust foundation for secure and efficient queries, as the `userId` can be used as a query filter, which is then validated against the `request.auth.uid` in the rules.
